content:
Use these templates to identify and communicate accessibility issues in designs.  
Organized by POUR: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust.

---

#### Perceivable
- Ensure all [body text / headings / buttons] have a color contrast ratio of at least [4.5:1] against the [background / image behind it].
- Add [alt text / captions / labels] to describe [images / videos / icons] so everyone can understand them.
- Avoid using only [color / sound / animation] to show important [information / status / feedback].

---

#### Operable
- Make sure users can navigate through the site using only the [keyboard / tab key / arrow keys].
- Design [buttons / links / menus] that are large enough and easy to [click / tap / focus].”
- Give users enough time to [read / fill out / respond to] any [popup / timed section / quiz].

---

#### Understandable
- Write [instructions / labels / content] using clear and simple [language / vocabulary].
- Keep [navigation menus / buttons / layouts] consistent across all [pages / sections].
- If users make a mistake, show an [error message / alert] that explains how to [fix it / try again].

---

#### Robust
- Test the site on different [devices / browsers / screen sizes] to make sure it still works.
- Use proper [HTML tags / structure / code] so [screen readers / assistive tech] can read it correctly.
- Make sure all [interactive elements / forms / buttons] are usable with [assistive technologies / voice commands].

---
